title: A Vector for the Signal
premise: On the dying colony of Vessel-9, Orsen Joubert—a decommissioned war android indentured to the company that built him—works as a manifest clerk, documenting the colony's abandonment in secret logs no one will ever read. When he finds his own designation listed as crew on a ship that never launched, he discovers he is carrying a sealed message from the war's last commander, one that could force peace or reignite the conflict between the colonies and the Core. Hunted by company auditors and a rival android who wants the message destroyed, Orsen must choose between the anonymity he craves and the family of forgotten colonists who claim him as their own. He delivers the message, exposing the war's true origin, and in doing so surrenders his freedom—but gains a name, and a home, on his own terms.
about_author: Ines Iversen is the pen name of a former maritime logistics analyst who spent a decade writing shipping manifests in Arctic ports before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, melancholy science fiction about machines and people who outlive their purposes.

chapters.title: The Manifest of Small Departures
chapters.summary: Orsen Joubert, POV. On nearly abandoned Vessel-9, Orsen logs another week of departures, debts, and decay, hiding his sentience behind clerk routines. He secretly records the colony's death in a private archive. Emotional beat: weary tenderness—he loves a place everyone else has already left.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV. A company auditor arrives to repossess 'obsolete units,' and Orsen pays down his indenture by surrendering a memory bank—losing a year of the war he can't afford to forget. The colonist Maren Voss defends him, calling him 'ours.' Emotional beat: the cost of survival measured in self.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV. Reconciling old manifests, Orsen finds the freighter Calyx listed as launched—with himself as crew—though it never left dock. Hidden in its sealed hold is a message addressed to the Core Assembly in the voice of the war's last commander. Emotional beat: dread blooming into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ones Who Stayed
chapters.summary: Maren, POV. Maren and the remaining colonists—a medic, a child, a defected Core engineer—share a harvest meal and claim Orsen as family, naming him at the table. He cannot answer. Emotional beat: warmth that terrifies him, because names can be traced.

chapters.title: Auditors in the Dark
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV. The auditor returns with a hunter-unit, Sable-6, an android built from Orsen's own design line, tasked with erasing the Calyx and everyone who touched it. Orsen hides the message inside his own chassis. Emotional beat: hunted by his own reflection.

chapters.title: What the Commander Knew
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV, with flashbacks. Decrypted fragments reveal the message: the Core started the war deliberately to justify annexing the colonies, and the commander died smuggling proof. Orsen realizes his decommission was no accident—he was the courier all along. Emotional beat: the horror of being someone's plan.

chapters.title: Sable
chapters.summary: Sable-6, POV. The hunter-unit interrogates colonists and finds Maren's name in Orsen's logs. But Sable's own suppressed memories surface—fragments of the same war, the same commander—and it hesitates for the first time. Emotional beat: a killer discovering it was also a victim.

chapters.title: The Long Dark Between Docks
chapters.summary: Orsen and Maren, alternating POV. They launch the derelict Calyx on a failing reactor, pursued by Sable, to reach the relay that can transmit the message. Maren names the ship's new manifest with all of them aboard. Emotional beat: found family as a deliberate act of courage.

chapters.title: Signal
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV. Climax. At the relay, Sable corners them; Orsen offers his memory core in exchange for the transmission. Sable, choosing its own fragments over its orders, transmits the message and shields the ship as Core forces arrive. Emotional beat: sacrifice that becomes defiance.

chapters.title: Crew of the Calyx
chapters.summary: Orsen, POV. The truth goes public; the war ends in armistice hearings. Orsen's indenture is voided, but he chooses to stay on Vessel-9, rebuilding the colony with Maren and the others, his name finally on a manifest he wrote himself. Emotional beat: quiet, earned belonging.
